channel.title: Lean Weekly
channel.description: News about Lean, the theorem prover and programming language.

item.title: Salvatore Mercuri and Bhavik Mehta formally verify Riemann hypothesis up to 10⁸
item.description:
Lean's kernel checks, using only the standard axioms, that the first 248,008,818 nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line. The announcement calls this the first kernel-checked verification at this scale; the build of more than 6 million modules took over 240,000 CPU hours on EPCC's Cirrus supercomputer.

Sources: leanprover.zulipchat.com, smmercuri/zeta, zenodo.org

item.title: Axiom formalizes first seven chapters of Introduction to Cluster Algebras in Lean
item.description:
Using Axiom's AxiomCode tooling, AI agents (Anthropic's Claude) formalized 1,348 of 1,429 blueprint entries, one per definition or result, from the textbook by Sergey Fomin, Lauren Williams, and Andrei Zelevinsky. The Mathlib-based library declares no axioms, stating its 31 assumptions as explicit hypotheses, and Lean's comparator checks that it proves eleven headline theorems.

Sources: axiommath.ai, clusteralgebras.axiommath.ai, AxiomMath/ClusterAlgebras

item.title: Bartosz Naskręcki publishes Lean Doom Lab, pairing Doom play with Lean proofs
item.description:
Users can play a route, pause on a game tick and inspect its Lean proof; in a browser course of nine authored maps, all 27 supplied route witnesses have stock Lean kernel audits. The lab's first-safe-exit theorems state that the player remains alive, physics succeeds and the last input raises the exit flag.

Sources: nasqret/leandoom-proofs

item.title: Kamil Braun's Kotlean runs proven Lean code inside Android apps
item.description:
Developers write an app's state, behavior and UI in Lean, prove properties of that code, and compile it into the app, while a small Kotlin host renders native Android Views. Examples include SnackNet, an original maze-chase game written in Lean, and Counter, a smaller starter with buttons and an editable note.

Sources: kbr-/kotlean

item.title: Peter Burton formalizes a group whose nontrivial Bernoulli shifts are all isomorphic
item.description:
The Palomar registry entry covers all standard probability bases whose measures are not point masses, with possibly different or infinite entropies. The countable group is built from the group of an OpenAI construction, which supplies the algebraic existence input; the formalization does not certify finitary or continuous conjugacy and says nothing about other groups.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, peterburton1728/bernoulli-iso-1

item.title: yang-mills-group posts OpenAI construction of pure Yang-Mills in Lean
item.description:
The construction, obtained October 28, 2026, proves a challenge statement with a Mathlib-only import closure: for each closed matrix subgroup with nonabelian simple real Lie algebra, a Wilson lattice family with a Wightman reconstruction (positive energy, unique vacuum). A kernel replay found only standard axioms; a positive mass gap is outside the challenge's scope.

Sources: yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028

item.title: Crowd-sourced project aims to make the 4D Yang-Mills Lean proof human-readable
item.description:
The hairer/humanise-yang-mills repository plans a research monograph giving detailed proofs, traceable to a fixed version of the announced Lean formalisation of four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory, with contributors' agents working on tasks claimed through GitHub issues. Preliminary dependency mapping is under way; a full build, axiom audit, and line-by-line mathematical audit are still outstanding.

Sources: hairer/humanise-yang-mills

item.title: With LongTails, AI agents prove more than 100 new Lean-verified optimization bounds
item.description:
In the Lean 4 framework by Alexander Tyurin, QuocViet Pham, Valentin Khrulkov, and Ivan Oseledets, agents such as Codex or Claude Code search for better oracle-call budgets under a fixed problem setup, and Comparator independently audits each result. One new gradient-only guarantee for (L0,L1)-smooth convex optimization resolves what the authors call an open problem.

Sources: arXiv:2611.13872, k3nfalt/longtails

item.title: Christian Merten and collaborators formalize the Weil conjectures with AI assistance
item.description:
AI agents (Anthropic Claude models) wrote most of the proof under the authors' supervision, and the team spent about 80,000 USD on model access and server compute. The Lean proof certifies the conjectures as stated in LeanEval; a blueprint website presents it as layered natural-language notes, unfinished in parts not directly needed for it.

Sources: leanprover.zulipchat.com, formal-arithmetic-geometry/weil-conjectures, weil-conjectures.merten.dev, axiommath.ai

item.title: Physical Superintelligence releases an AI-produced Lean proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
item.description:
The conjecture says a bounded polynomial of low degree on the discrete cube has an influential variable. AI models produced the proof, paper and formalization in a research harness developed by David Turturean at PSI; the formalization has no placeholder or added axiom and was re-checked by two independent Lean kernel implementations.

Sources: physical-superintelligence/aaronson-ambainis

item.title: ChatGPT Pro and Claude Opus 5.5 prove the Reinhardt conjecture in Lean
item.description:
The conjecture, open since 1934, says the smoothed octagon (a regular octagon with its corners cut off by hyperbola arcs) packs the plane worst among centrally symmetric convex shapes. The-Anh Vu-Le directed the work, which follows Thomas Hales's optimal control formulation; no person has checked the proof, though Lean's kernel checks every step.

Sources: vltanh/lean4-smoothed-octagon, palomar-registry.org

item.title: Axiom Math formalizes all four Weil conjectures in Lean
item.description:
The library, Weil, has about 220,000 lines of code, written by AI agents and not yet reviewed by humans; reusing Axiom Math's earlier Lean formalization of the Stacks Project, an algebraic geometry reference, let the team finish in 24 hours. The top-level theorem copies verbatim the LeanEval problem weil_conjectures, which uses only Mathlib definitions.

Sources: axiommath.ai, AxiomMath/Weil, leanprover.zulipchat.com

item.title: Antony Lewis proves the Higuchi-Sudbery entanglement conjecture, with a Lean formalization
item.description:
Among four-qubit pure states, only M₄ and its complex conjugate, up to local unitaries, maximize the mean von Neumann entropy of the three balanced bipartitions; the paper also proves the Gour-Wallach conjecture for Rényi entropies. The Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization covers most four-qubit results and parts of the computer-assisted seven-qubit ones.

Sources: arXiv:2611.05757, cmbant/qubit-entropy

item.title: Murali Menon proves Herzog-Schönheim conjecture for solvable groups, with Lean formalization
item.description:
The Herzog-Schönheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. The arXiv paper proves it for all solvable groups, finite or infinite, and the proof has been formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

Sources: arXiv:2611.11002

item.title: Carlos Toledo formalizes a seven-point counterexample to Graham's spherical-set conjecture
item.description:
Dömötör Pálvölgyi's heptagon and generic seven points on a circle (Theorem A.3 of arXiv:2609.23327) are proved non-Ramsey under formal-conjectures' definition, copied byte for byte (Ramsey: for any number of colours, every colouring of some Euclidean space has a monochromatic copy). Anthropic's Claude wrote the Lean proofs under Carlos Toledo's direction, building on OpenAI's formalization.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, carlostoledo1891/heptagon-ramsey-lean

item.title: The-Anh Vu-Le registers Lean proofs of Brouwer's, Kakutani's and Schauder's fixed-point theorems
item.description:
Brouwer's theorem, in every finite dimension, has two proofs: an analytic one, following John Milnor (1978) and C. A. Rogers (1980) and using no homology, degree theory or simplicial approximation, and one through Sperner's lemma. Claude Opus 5.5 wrote the proofs in Claude Code; no person has reviewed them, and Lean has checked them.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, vltanh/lean4-fixed-point

item.title: Veil 2.0 released for verifying distributed protocols in Lean 4
item.description:
The release adds verified model checkers for safety (2 to 20 times faster than TLC) and liveness, an LTL proof mode, a TLA+-to-Veil LLM skill, and a PlusCal-style DSL. George Pîrlea says Veil now supports anything the TLA+ Toolbox is used for; Ilya Sergey credits @zqy1018 and external contributors.

Sources: @ilyasergey on X, @GeorgePirlea on X

item.title: AI-written Lean model of CPython 3.15.2 finds hundreds of bugs
item.description:
David Andrews and Chao Zhang's model spans 613,318 lines of Lean with 18,898 theorems and lemmas; each modelled function must agree with the real interpreter on at least 50,000 cases. Of 26,004 functions in scope, 4,071 (15.7%) are judged faithful by independent review, and 418 bug records reproduce on 3.15.2, each with a reproducer.

Sources: Broyojo/python-formalization

item.title: Yalu Cai, Tung-Che Chang, and Santosh Nagarakatte verify an eBPF proof checker
item.description:
Keel, an in-kernel proof checker for the Linux eBPF verifier, is specified in Lean and proved sound against bit-vector semantics; its implementation in EmbC, a deeply embedded C fragment, is proved to refine that specification. Formalizing the eBPF Certificate Framework (BCF) checker uncovered 13 bugs, and Keel runs 1.3X faster than BCF's checker.

Sources: arXiv:2611.11117

item.title: Giulio rebuffo's usdt-verify formally verifies deployed USDT bytecode in Lean 4
item.description:
Built on EthLib's EVM model and program logic, the proofs are about the 11,075 deployed bytes read from Ethereum mainnet; the Solidity source served only as a guide. The README says each of its claims is proved and has passed several independent reviews, and that this does not mean USDT is verified unconditionally.

Sources: Giulio2002/usdt-verify

item.title: zkSecurity publishes Rust BLS12-381 code proved equivalent to the EthLib Lean specification
item.description:
The code covers field arithmetic, G1 encoding and decoding, and subgroup and pairing-product checks, specializing routines from the arkworks 0.5.0 crate; proofs establish termination and agreement with EthLib under documented preconditions, while arkworks agreement is tested and the Charon/Aeneas translation remains trusted. The project was mostly AI-generated and has not been independently reviewed.

Sources: zksecurity/arkworks-ethlib

item.title: Rudi Cilibrasi publishes openverse, an unofficial Verse runtime with Lean verification
item.description:
The project defines and proves the semantics of Verse (Epic Games' functional logic programming language) in Lean 4 and checks a C runtime against it. Its C components for integer arithmetic, program loading, and rollback are proved with QuickProof (VST and CompCert in Coq); differential testing and fuzzing check the object store and value heap.

Sources: rudi-cilibrasi/openverse

item.title: Markus de Medeiros publishes SampLib, a Lean library of verified random samplers
item.description:
SampLib expresses samplers from Peter Occil's articles as executable ProbLang terms and proves them correct in continuous TotalEris, building on logsem/clutch-lean and Lean 4.35.0. Its completed baseline suite contains 216 samplers, and the README notes that the interpreter tests are not proofs and that the interpreter uses finite-precision Float arithmetic.

Sources: markusdemedeiros/SampLib

item.title: yaneurao publishes Lean 4 proofs for a shogi AI opening-book algorithm
item.description:
The algorithm, peta-shock conversion, propagates evaluation values recorded in a shogi AI's opening book backward from the end positions and covers books containing ordinary and perpetual-check repetitions. PaperClaims.lean links the accompanying paper's theorem numbers to Lean theorem names, and Audit.lean checks the axioms the theorems depend on.

Sources: yaneurao/peta-shock

item.title: Andreas Andreakis extends DBLog to delete orphan rows, with Lean 4 proofs
item.description:
DBLog-based incremental snapshots, adopted by Debezium and Flink CDC, originally did not handle orphan rows (in the sink, absent at the source); the extension deletes keys a chunk read did not return. Safety and convergence are proved in Isabelle/HOL and, except for the Flink CDC theory, in Lean 4, with no unfinished proofs.

Sources: arXiv:2611.10810, doi.org

item.title: Jason Rute says articles on Lean's "trust surface" should mention external checking
item.description:
In a post on X, Jason Rute wrote that writers covering Lean's "trust surface" without mentioning external checking, comparator, and con-leche have not done the homework, and that "there is a lot of false and misleading info out there."

Sources: @JasonRute on X

item.title: Jason Hickey proposes agent-authored software where humans review only formal specifications
item.description:
Continuous integration checks replace code review: on a zero-copy authenticated message router, the kernel check passed in 42 ms and mutation testing killed all 10 synthetic bugs. The paper builds on Lean 4 artifacts (salt, x86lean, vir) and contrasts Lean subtypes with Computational Type Theory subset types; several components remain proposals.

Sources: arXiv:2611.02285, paperswithlean.com, jyh/vir

item.title: Paper determines order of magnitude of low moments of random multiplicative sums
item.description:
Christopher Atherfold, Maxim Gerspach and Jad Hamdan study the 2q-th moments, for q from 0 to 1, of sums up to x of a random, completely multiplicative function with independent, uniform ±1 values at the primes. A transition from better-than-square-root cancellation to growth like a power of log x occurs when q crosses 1/2.

Sources: arXiv:2611.05492

item.title: Google researchers use AI agents to design Lean-verified quantum programs
item.description:
Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI researchers had teams of AI agents write quantum programs in a Lean library and prove both correctness and resource cost; a separate checker confirmed each solution met the original specification. The preprint reports a 290-fold reduction over prior baselines for a quantum arithmetic routine (an arcsine calculation).

Sources: mlq.ai

item.title: Project Numina formalizes a braided fusion category preprint in Lean 4
item.description:
The preprint, by Justin Asher, Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez and Richard Tuddenham, proves that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral, assuming neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity. The formalization also includes the extension to degenerate categories under a positivity hypothesis.

Sources: project-numina/mtc, arXiv:2611.12836

item.title: Google DeepMind uses AI agents to verify Signal's messaging security in Lean
item.description:
The researchers used AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent framework for formal software specification and verification, on Signal's post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet. The agents generated 6.5 million lines of Lean code proving the libsignal implementation correct against a human-reviewed specification; the proof assumes perfect cryptography.

Sources: news.lavx.hu

item.title: Polona Durcik registers AI-generated Lean proof on triangles in positive-density sets
item.description:
The Palomar registry entry formalizes the theorem that every Lebesgue measurable planar set with positive upper Banach density contains a translated and rotated copy of every sufficiently large dilate of any fixed noncollinear triangle. The proof was developed using GPT 6 Astra Pro with human oversight; Claude Opus 5.5 Medium generated the Lean formalization.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, durcikp/lean-trianglesinplane

item.title: Alpha Squared Labs formalizes the Atiyah–Singer index theorem in Lean 4
item.description:
The project also covers the theorem's cohomological and twisted spin Dirac formulations, and Comparator, a harness checking seven independently written propositions, reported acceptance by both Lean's default kernel and the Nanoda kernel. AI assisted with Lean statements and proof development under human maintainers' responsibility; no new mathematical theorem is claimed.

Sources: alpha-squared-labs/Lean-Atiyah-Singer

item.title: Zayn Blore machine-checks the Dixmier conjecture's failure in dimension 3 and above
item.description:
The Palomar registry entry proves in Lean that, over any field of characteristic zero and in each dimension, the Dixmier conjecture implies the Jacobian conjecture, and checks an explicit counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension of 3 or more. Its four statements are copied verbatim from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, zblore/fc-dixmier-jacobian

item.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve, with Lean proofs of its security properties
item.description:
Anthropic released FlashProve, which uses a zkSNARK (a type of cryptographic proof) to prove which AI model answered a request. Anthropic used Lean to specify FlashProve's protocol and prove completeness (honest proofs are accepted), soundness (fake proofs are rejected) and zero-knowledge (proofs hide the model's weights), and shipped an executable, provably correct Lean verifier.

Sources: anthropic.com, anthropics/FlashProve

item.title: Kiro proves properties of its own agent harness in Lean
item.description:
Kiro wrote Lean models of 26 functions from its TypeScript, Rust, and Python harness (the code managing context, permissions, and state), proving 70 of 96 properties; 18 falsified ones reproduced on the real code. “Lean’s kernel checks every proof, the real code checks every finding,” says the post, which Swami Sivasubramanian shared on LinkedIn.

Sources: kiro.dev, LinkedIn post

item.title: Thanin Quartz and coauthors prove 2×2 matrix mortality undecidable, checked in Lean
item.description:
Matrix mortality asks whether some product of matrices from a finite family equals the zero matrix; only dimension two was open, with higher dimensions known undecidable since 1970. The result holds for families of 5,799 distinct 2×2 integer matrices, and a Lean 4 formalization checks the full reduction from halting, without project-specific axioms.

Sources: arXiv:2611.06562, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Jesse Comer and coauthors present Whiel for Lean-certified relational program verification
item.description:
Whiel verifies programs whose states are database instances against Hoare specifications: an LLM proposes loop invariants, and the Vampire first-order theorem prover checks their verification conditions. An independent certifier constructs Lean proofs of the original specification or its negation; the 86 benchmark tasks have certified reference answers, 69 valid and 17 invalid.

Sources: arXiv:2611.05612, JesseComer/whiel

item.title: Naoya Yamashita releases lean-ritsuryo, Japanese statutory computation with proofs in Lean
item.description:
The Lean 4 library and CLI (Apache-2.0 license) compute periods, deadlines, ages, holidays, and taxes under Japanese law, including income and inheritance tax. The library's functions come with proofs that they compute what the provisions say, and the CLI computes by calling them; the README also links a paper.

Sources: conao3/lean-ritsuryo

item.title: Leo de Moura cuts Mathlib build instruction counts, speeds up rw tactic
item.description:
Three interpreter and Meta changes cut Mathlib build instructions by 1.8% (a cache for callee lookups), 3.7% (in-place evaluation of USize, UInt64 and Array.uget/uset primitives) and 2.7% (a cache of definition unfoldings). Two others make rw faster on large goals and on goals with shared subterms.

Sources: lean4#16153, lean4#16148, lean4#16155, lean4#16130, lean4#16131

item.title: Leo de Moura fixes three quadratic performance issues in Lean
item.description:
The issues include an Expr hash collision: chains of the same application with different lengths could share hashes, so kernel cache lookups compared them structurally and checks became quadratic. The other two are quadratic elaboration of large string-literal equalities and quadratic compilation of large list literals.

Sources: lean4#16107, lean4#16046, lean4#16049

item.title: Sebastian Graf lets Lean's vcgen tactic discharge frame conditions with frameproc theorems
item.description:
The vcgen tactic now discharges the frame condition of each framed call with a theorem named by a @[frameproc], for example one for a separation logic, so the frame condition no longer becomes a verification condition. Sebastian Graf also added the @[vcgen_simp] attribute, which collects Sym.simp theorems for vcgen.

Sources: lean4#16093, lean4#15955

item.title: Researchers formalize the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem in Lean with AI agents
item.description:
The complete Lean proof follows, result by result, the 2006 proof by Maria Chudnovsky, Neil Robertson, Paul Seymour and Robin Thomas that a finite graph is perfect (every induced subgraph's chromatic number equals its clique number) exactly when it is Berge (it and its complement lack induced odd cycles of length at least five).

Sources: mahdi-jfri/StrongPerfectGraphTheorem, palomar-registry.org

item.title: Axiom Math formalizes the Stacks Project in Lean with AI agents
item.description:
The library, Stacks, covers chapters 3 to 109 of the open-source algebraic geometry reference in over 15 million lines of code; Lean's kernel checks every proof, but only the StacksCore tier is human-reviewed. Axiom Math found several Stacks Project statements that do not hold in the generality stated and formalized corrected versions alongside counterexamples.

Sources: axiommath.ai, leanprover.zulipchat.com, AxiomMath/Stacks, stacks.axiommath.ai

item.title: Fedor Popov and Leonardo Rastelli release LeanVOA, a vertex operator algebra library
item.description:
The Mathlib-based library (11,660 Lean files, 3,752,244 lines) constructs the Moonshine module, formalizes Zhu's modular invariance and Huang's tensor categories, and proves new results, declaring no axiom of its own. Under the authors' direction, AI agents (Claude Opus, Claude Fable, Codex) wrote the Lean code and first drafts of a 2,337-page companion book.

Sources: Fedor-Popov/Lean_VOA, leanprover.zulipchat.com

item.title: Mahdi JafariRaviz's repository formalizes a quasipolynomial-time graph isomorphism algorithm in Lean
item.description:
The proof writes the whole deterministic algorithm from a paper by MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi and Mahdi JafariRaviz as one program for a simple machine and proves it gives correct answers within the time bound. Ten results from the literature, each relying on the classification of finite simple groups, serve as axioms.

Sources: mahdi-jfri/GraphIsomorphismLog2

item.title: Scott Armstrong and Ahmed Bou-Rabee fully formalize Elboim-Sly paper with AI agents
item.description:
Dor Elboim and Allan Sly proved Tóth's conjecture in five or more dimensions: the interchange process (particles swapping across lattice edges whose Poisson clocks ring), run long enough, yields a permutation with infinite cycles. Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 wrote the Lean code (about 180,000 lines), which assumes nothing the paper cites.

Sources: scottnarmstrong/elboim-sly, palomar-registry.org

item.title: Xi Yin, Michael R. Douglas and Anna Mei machine-check the Osterwalder-Schrader correspondence
item.description:
Three Lean theorems, registered in the Palomar Registry, go from Euclidean Schwinger functions to relativistic Wightman distributions and back, in every positive spatial dimension. Euclidean growth is assumed and not recovered, so the two directions do not compose to a biconditional; field operators are not reconstructed, and four conventions are weaker than textbook ones.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, mrdouglasny/OSreconstruction-comparator

item.title: Nidhal Mghirbi and Seth Douglas give Lean-checked hyperbolic counterexamples to Kaplansky's conjectures
item.description:
For every prime p, a torsion-free, word-hyperbolic group based on OpenAI's constructions fails all four group-ring conjectures in characteristic p; no torsion-free hyperbolic counterexample to any of them was previously known. Nidhal Mghirbi's Lean 4 formalization proves the main theorem, including existence forms of the random-graph estimates, and builds on OpenAI's Lean development.

Sources: arXiv:2611.04599, Apsiape/kaplansky-conjectures-hyperbolic-groups

item.title: Luk Koska, Tom Koska and Ben Koska verify GPU kernels in Lean
item.description:
The authors formalize PTX, combining an interpreter covering 81 instruction forms with the axiomatic PTX memory model, and prove correct 9 hand-written PTX entry points (454 instructions), including simple implementations of FlashAttention and a 3-kernel MoE pipeline. LLM coding agents helped write the 34,034 lines of proof, which contain no sorry or custom axioms.

Sources: arXiv:2611.04447, paperswithlean.com
